text: Today I took my child to get a tooth extracted, not knowing there was no pediatric dentist. The male doctor was very rude, scolding my child, covering his mouth to stop him from crying, and pointing at him, accusing him of lying when he said it would hurt. I told him my child has developmental delays and is autistic, but he said that wasn't relevant and continued to scold and point at my child. I felt so sorry for my child; he's very timid and easily startled, but he endured until the procedure was finished. Afterward, the doctor told me to come to a pediatric dentist next time, as if he was unwilling to treat my child. If you, doctor, read this, please reflect on your behavior. You've made a child afraid of dentists for life. I am very upset that I took my child to this clinic. Please use more respectful language with your patients. We paid for this treatment; you are a healthcare provider, you should behave better. Please consider this.

text:
I've been here for many treatments and various issues. My first visit was incredibly impressive. The doctor was very attentive and listened carefully to my oral health concerns—something I'd never experienced before. The doctor was very friendly and approachable, making me feel comfortable and not afraid at all.
And every subsequent visit has been equally impressive. All the doctors here are excellent; they are gentle, polite, and friendly. The assistants are also very polite and friendly.
The clinic itself is clean and spacious, with three examination rooms and one X-ray room.
There might be a few minor drawbacks, but personally, I'd overlook them. Since the doctors provide such good treatment, everything else is great.
